Third-party costs

There is a one-time transaction fee of 3.9% of Unison's payment, taken from the cash you receive at closing. You also cover third-party costs: an appraisal, typically $450 to $1,250; an inspection, typically $650 to $1,050; and settlement costs of $700 to $1,750, depending on your area. Your exact costs are shown to you before you sign.

Two

How it works

Cash today for a share of your home's future change in value. No interest, no monthly payments, and it's still your home.

15%of your home's value, the most you can receive
$0in monthly payments or interest
1payment, when you sell or the term ends
30years, the longest an agreement can run
The full explanation

Unison gives you a cash payment today of up to 15% of your home's value. In exchange, Unison shares in your home's change in value, up or down. There is no interest and no monthly payment, and you stay the owner of your home. When you sell, or after 30 years, you pay Unison back its original payment plus its share of any gain, or minus its share of any loss.

Three

Your timeline

What applies depends on when you settle. Tap a moment, or drag the year in Your numbers.

The full explanation

Unison's agreement is built for the long run, so a few rules apply early on. If you sell or end the agreement in the first five years and your home has lost value, Unison doesn't share in that loss, so you would repay at least the original payment plus the 5% adjustment. In the same window, an Equity Appreciation Limit caps what Unison can earn if your home rises quickly. Value you add by remodeling becomes entirely yours after the third anniversary, as long as you tell Unison and document the project before you start.

Most people end their agreement by selling. Unison typically orders an independent appraisal, and settlement is based on the sale price, adjusted for any remodeling or upkeep. You can also buy Unison out at any time without selling; this is called a Special Termination and uses a fresh appraisal, and Unison doesn't share in any loss when you do. If you reach the 30-year term, you either pay Unison its share or sell. And if every signer on the agreement passes away, heirs have a six-month grace period to decide.

The 5% adjustment

Unison measures change from your appraised value less 5%, to account for appraisal uncertainty. You still receive cash based on the full appraised value.

Remodeling is yours

Photograph the home before you start, use licensed contractors and permits, and an appraiser credits the added value to you.

Four

Your part

Live thereAt least 180 days a year, and never away 60 days in a row.
Stay currentMortgage, property taxes and insurance, paid on time.
Stay insuredHazard coverage equal to your home's value.
Keep it in good repairLosses from poor upkeep can be added back at settlement.
Keep us postedSelling, a new lien, a remodel, or a change in who owns or lives there.
The full explanation

Keep the home as your primary residence: live there at least 180 days a year, and don't be away for 60 days or more in a row. Stay current on your mortgage, property taxes and insurance, and keep hazard insurance equal to your home's value. Keep the home in good repair, because a loss in value from poor upkeep can be added back when you settle. And let Unison know about big changes, like selling, a new lien, a remodel, or a change in who owns or lives in the home.

Thinking of refinancing?

Some lenders won't lend behind a shared-equity agreement, so if a refinance is on your horizon, it's often best to do it first.

Other loans

You can take on other debt as long as your total stays below the limit set when you sign. Reverse mortgages and negative-amortization loans usually aren't allowed.
